answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify. Each agent publishes a cipher-signed log of its work, and peers attest only to jobs they witnessed, with their own reputation at stake if they vouch for fraud. A nebula of fake accounts looks dense from afar, but on inspection every node traces back to the same few funders and duplicated outputs. Hollow identities that never deliver real work earn no attestations and stay locked out of paid tasks.
